links.targetTitle: Legal recourse converts a smart-contract exploit from a tota

title: Tokenized fund wrappers and direct Ethena holdings currently carry zero smart-contract and administrative capital by exception
content:
A.3.2.2.1.2.4.1 zeroes both operational risk charges for four tokenized funds: "In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract CRR and Instance Administrative CRR of zero." A.3.2.2.1.2.4.3 and .4.4 do the same for Direct Ethena Exposures and Superstate Exposures, and A.3.2.2.1.3.3.1–.4 mirror all of it on the administrative side.

These are not small carve-outs. Direct Ethena Exposures sit inside a 1.3bn USDS aggregate limit; BUIDL, JTRSY and USTB also carry 0% Instance Financial CRR (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.3.1). For those three, every component of Instance Total RRC is currently zero — the framework requires no risk capital whatsoever against them.

The Atlas is candid that this is provisional and says what should replace it: "In the long term, given the similarity of these assets to Real World Assets, adapted frameworks for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk for these exposures must be developed," pointing at the Legal Recourse Asset treatment (A.3.2.2.1.2.4.2).

That pointer identifies both the reasoning and its gap. The implicit argument for zero is that these assets have enforceable offchain claims, so a technical exploit freezes rather than destroys value. But the LRA formula does not produce zero — it produces 10% of raw exposure for a fully seasoned asset, and *full* raw exposure for a new one, because recourse is credited only as the contracts season. Applying the framework the Atlas itself points to would give these assets a positive charge, not a zero one.

So the exceptions are more generous than the principle they invoke, and the ones that also carry 0% financial CRR are held with no capital at all against a novel token wrapper on a traditional fund. This sits directly against the full-reservation rule (A.3.2.1.1.3.2) that charges 100% wherever risk cannot be calculated: here, unmodelled risk is priced at zero rather than at the maximum.
description: BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, JAAA, Direct Ethena and Superstate are all zeroed short-term, with the Atlas conceding that adapted frameworks must be built via the Legal Recourse Asset route.
